Hi Mel, I can't diagnose anything without seeing your leg, but what you're describing (stiff first thing, sore a few cm up from the heel, eases once you warm up, big jump in k's) is a really common pattern when an Achilles has been overloaded. No pop or sudden onset is a good sign too.

One correction to the advice above: I'd steer clear of stretching it hard till it burns. That tends to compress and irritate the tendon rather than settle it. Cortisone near the Achilles isn't something I'd go for either, as it can weaken the tendon.

What usually works better is loading it. Not full rest, not pushing through.

On sore days or bad mornings, do isometric holds. Rise up onto your toes and hold for 30 to 45 seconds, 4 or 5 rounds.

Otherwise do slow, heavy calf raises, about 3 seconds up and 3 seconds down, 3 sets of 8 to 12, every second day. Add weight (a backpack works) once they feel easy. Heel drops off a step are fine, but heavy slow raises have better evidence these days.

For pain, up to about 3/10 while you're loading it is ok, as long as it's settled by the next morning. If it's worse the next day, back off. Limping around the office after a run tells me the volume is a bit much for now, so keep runs shorter, flat and easy for a couple of weeks and build back up gradually. You've got plenty of time before Rottnest.

If it's not settling in 3 to 4 weeks, see any sports physio near you in Bayswater.

If you ever get a sudden pop, a feeling like a kick in the back of the leg, or can't push off, stop running and the calf work and get it checked urgently that same day (GP or ED). That could be a rupture.

Last thing for anyone reading: some antibiotics can affect tendons, so if you're on a course and your tendons start getting sore, tell whoever prescribed it.

Good luck, keep us posted.

Kaz
